# Comparison to n8n

Covers dimension 14 (Comparison to n8n). n8n analysis at
[research/n8n/](../../n8n/). Sources referenced in [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Fundamental Difference

Inngest and n8n are **not directly competitive** — they serve different
developer personas and solve different problems:

- **n8n** is a visual-first workflow automation platform (Zapier competitor)
  with optional code. Founded 2019, $2.5B valuation, 150K+ GitHub stars [44].
- **Inngest** is a code-first durable execution platform (Temporal competitor)
  with event-driven architecture. Founded 2021, ~$30M funding, ~5.2K GitHub
  stars [38][21].

## Dimension-by-Dimension Comparison

### 1. What It Is

| Aspect | Inngest | n8n |
|--------|---------|-----|
| Architecture | Event-driven durable execution [7] | Visual workflow graphs [44] |
| Primary interface | Code SDKs (TS, Python, Go) [33] | Drag-and-drop canvas + code nodes [44] |
| Core abstraction | Step functions with memoization [7] | Node graph (JSON-serialized) [44] |
| Target audience | Developers writing code [32] | Mixed: no-code to pro-code [44] |

### 2. Licensing

| Aspect | Inngest | n8n |
|--------|---------|-----|
| Server license | SSPL with DOSP → Apache 2.0 after 3 years [14] | Sustainable Use License [44] |
| OSI-compliant | No (SSPL rejected by OSI) | No (custom license) [44] |
| SDK license | Apache 2.0 [39] | N/A (monorepo) |
| Personal use | Permitted under SSPL [14] | Permitted under SUL [44] |

**Assessment:** Equivalent — both source-available, neither OSI-approved.
Inngest has a clearer path to full open source (automatic Apache 2.0 after
3 years) [14].

### 3. Self-Hosting

| Aspect | Inngest | n8n |
|--------|---------|-----|
| Deployment | Single binary, Docker, Helm [1] | Docker, npm, Helm [44] |
| Default storage | SQLite + in-memory Redis [1] | SQLite (default) or PostgreSQL [44] |
| Production storage | PostgreSQL + Redis [1] | PostgreSQL + Redis (queue mode) [44] |
| Resource requirements | Not documented [1] | ~170-256 MB RAM idle [44] |
| Single-host viable | Yes [1] | Yes [44] |

**Assessment:** Both viable on a single workstation. n8n has published resource
numbers; Inngest does not. n8n's queue mode with Redis is similar to Inngest's
Redis recommendation for production.

### 4. CLI/Script Execution

| Aspect | Inngest | n8n |
|--------|---------|-----|
| Dedicated CLI node | **No** — use subprocess in step.run() | **Yes** — Execute Command node [44] |
| Stdout/stderr capture | Manual via subprocess [22] | Automatic in Execute Command [44] |
| Code execution | In-app code via SDK | JavaScript/Python Code nodes [44] |
| Shell command UX | Write wrapper code | Visual drag-and-drop |

**Assessment:** **n8n is stronger.** n8n's Execute Command node runs shell
commands natively with automatic output capture. Inngest requires writing
language-native subprocess wrappers — functional but more effort, with no
documented examples.

### 5. Credential Management

| Aspect | Inngest | n8n |
|--------|---------|-----|
| Secret storage | Environment variables on user infrastructure | Built-in AES256-encrypted store [44] |
| Credential UI | None — env vars only | Dashboard UI for credential management [44] |
| Credential isolation | Secrets never reach Inngest [7] | Credentials stored in n8n database [44] |
| E2E encryption | Optional via SDK middleware [19] | AES256 at rest [44] |

**Assessment:** **n8n is stronger** for convenience (UI, AES256 encryption).
Inngest's model (secrets stay on user infrastructure) is architecturally
cleaner for the PA credential isolation requirement, since the engine literally
cannot access application secrets.

### 6. Scheduling

| Aspect | Inngest | n8n |
|--------|---------|-----|
| Cron support | Yes, with `TZ=` prefix [3] | Yes, via Schedule Trigger node [44] |
| Timezone handling | TZ= prefix in cron expression [3] | Timezone selector in UI [44] |
| Minimum interval | 1 minute [3] | 1 minute [44] |
| Durable delays | step.sleep() up to 1 year [26] | Wait node (limited duration) [44] |
| One-off scheduling | Event ts field [26] | Via external trigger [44] |

**Assessment:** Inngest is stronger for durable delays (up to 1 year).
Equivalent for basic cron scheduling.

### 7. API for Workflow Management

| Aspect | Inngest | n8n |
|--------|---------|-----|
| Workflow CRUD via API | **No** — functions are code [7] | **Yes** — full CRUD via REST API [44] |
| Trigger via API | Yes — POST events [15] | Yes — webhook or API trigger [44] |
| Query run status | Yes — GET /v1/events/{id}/runs [15] | Yes — executions API [44] |
| List workflows | MCP tools only (dev server) [13] | Yes — workflows API [44] |

**Assessment:** **n8n is stronger.** n8n treats workflows as API-managed
resources with full CRUD. Inngest functions are code artifacts that must be
deployed — no API-based creation or modification.

### 8. Webhook Support

| Aspect | Inngest | n8n |
|--------|---------|-----|
| Webhook creation | Dashboard UI + transform function [5] | Visual Webhook node, auto-URL [44] |
| Transform required | Yes — JavaScript transform function [5] | No — direct JSON passthrough [44] |
| Auth options | Event key + signing key [24] | Basic, header, JWT [44] |
| Testing | Dashboard transform tester [5] | UI test with recorded data [44] |

**Assessment:** **n8n is stronger** for webhook UX — drop a Webhook node,
get a URL, no transform code needed. Inngest requires writing JavaScript
transform functions even if the rest of your code is Python.

### 9. Execution History

| Aspect | Inngest | n8n |
|--------|---------|-----|
| Automatic tracing | Yes, zero-config [8] | Yes, per-execution logs [44] |
| Per-step detail | Input/output/error/headers/metadata tabs [8] | Per-node input/output [44] |
| Timeline view | Waterfall with queue delays [8] | Execution timeline [44] |
| OpenTelemetry | Extended traces (TS SDK 3.44.5+) [8] | Not mentioned [44] |
| Retention | 7 days (Pro), 90 days (Enterprise) [10] | Configurable (pruning settings) [44] |

**Assessment:** **Inngest is stronger.** Waterfall traces with queue delay
breakdown, retry attempt visibility, and OpenTelemetry support provide deeper
observability than n8n's execution logs.

### 10. Retry and Error Handling

| Aspect | Inngest | n8n |
|--------|---------|-----|
| Default retries | 4 (5 total attempts) [2] | 0 (must enable) [44] |
| Backoff strategy | Exponential with jitter (default) [2] | Configurable per node [44] |
| Per-step retries | Independent counters [2] | Per-node setting [44] |
| Custom retry timing | RetryAfterError [2] | Wait before retry setting [44] |
| Failure handlers | onFailure + system events [9] | Error workflow trigger [44] |
| DLQ / Replay | Built-in Replay (all plans) [29] | Manual re-execution [44] |

**Assessment:** **Inngest is stronger.** Default-on retries with exponential
backoff, per-step independence, and the Replay feature for bulk failure
recovery are more robust than n8n's opt-in retry configuration.

### 11. AI/LLM Integration

| Aspect | Inngest | n8n |
|--------|---------|-----|
| LLM nodes | step.ai.infer/wrap [11] | 70+ LangChain nodes [44] |
| Agent framework | AgentKit (TS, early access) [12] | AI Agent node (GA) [44] |
| Vector stores | None built-in | 12 backends [44] |
| MCP support | Dev Server MCP (8 tools) [13] | MCP server/client [44] |
| RAG | No built-in support | Full pipeline [44] |

**Assessment:** **n8n is far stronger** for AI/LLM integration. 70+
LangChain nodes, 12 vector stores, RAG pipelines, and a GA agent node vs
Inngest's step-level primitives and early-access AgentKit. However, for this
use case, AI integration in the workflow engine is not required — the PA is
the LLM layer.

### 12. Community and Maturity

| Metric | Inngest | n8n |
|--------|---------|-----|
| GitHub stars | ~5,200 [38] | 150,000+ [44] |
| Founded | 2021 [21] | 2019 [44] |
| Funding/valuation | ~$30M [20][21] | $2.5B valuation [44] |
| Team size | Unknown | 67 [44] |
| Revenue | Unknown | $40M [44] |
| Named customers | ~20+ [28] | Thousands [44] |

**Assessment:** **n8n is far more mature** by community metrics. ~29x more
GitHub stars, ~83x higher valuation, established revenue.

### 13. Summary Table

| Dimension | Inngest | n8n | Winner |
|-----------|---------|-----|--------|
| CLI execution | Subprocess in step.run() | Execute Command node | **n8n** |
| Credential isolation | Env vars, never reaches engine | AES256-encrypted store | **Inngest** (for PA isolation) |
| Self-hosting | Single binary, zero-dep default | Docker, well-documented | Equivalent |
| API management | Event trigger + status query | Full workflow CRUD | **n8n** |
| Scheduling | Cron + durable delays to 1 year | Cron + Schedule Trigger | **Inngest** (durable delays) |
| Webhooks | Transform functions required | Drop-in webhook node | **n8n** |
| Execution history | Waterfall traces, OTEL | Per-node logs | **Inngest** |
| Retry/error handling | Default-on, per-step, Replay | Opt-in, per-node | **Inngest** |
| AI/LLM | Step primitives, AgentKit early | 70+ LangChain nodes, GA | **n8n** |
| Community | ~5.2K stars, $30M | 150K+ stars, $2.5B | **n8n** |

**Score: n8n 5, Inngest 4, Equivalent 1**

## Gaps and Limitations

- **Not a direct comparison** — these tools serve different use cases. Comparing
  them on the same dimensions is useful for this evaluation but doesn't reflect
  how either platform positions itself
- **n8n comparison data** from local analysis [44], not from a third-party
  comparative review
- **No migration path** between the two platforms
- **No performance comparison** data available
